status_summary: Executive Order 14163 (signed 2025-01-20) suspended refugee entry under the program effective 2025-01-27, with case-by-case exceptions and recurring 90-day reviews of whether to resume. On 2026-03-05 the Ninth Circuit, in Pacito v. Trump, found the President likely has authority to suspend refugee entry under 8 U.S.C. 1182(f), while affirming in part preliminary injunctions that require reception and placement services for refugees already in the country and preserve cooperative agreements with resettlement organizations (as reported by Jurist; the case remains at the preliminary injunction stage). The FY2026 presidential determination (signed 2025-09-30) set a ceiling of 7,500 allocated primarily to Afrikaners from South Africa under Executive Order 14204; an emergency determination signed 2026-05-21 raised the FY2026 ceiling to 17,500 for the same group, and the FY2027 determination (signed 2026-09-25) allows up to 17,500, again primarily Afrikaners. The Mandate recommended curtailment and did not recommend prioritizing any particular nationality or group, so the allocation to Afrikaners is an addition to what the Mandate described.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14163 suspended entry of refugees under the US Refugee Admissions Program effective 2025-01-27, allowed joint State-DHS case-by-case exceptions, and required reports every 90 days on whether resuming admissions serves US interests (published 2025-01-30).

Executive Order 14204, Addressing Egregious Actions of the Republic of South Africa, was published; later presidential determinations describe it as providing for resettlement of Afrikaners who are victims of unjust racial discrimination.

Presidential Determination 2025-13 set the FY2026 refugee ceiling at 7,500, allocated primarily to Afrikaners from South Africa, subject to Executive Orders 14161, 14163 and 14204 (published 2025-10-31).

The Ninth Circuit, in Pacito v. Trump, held that the President likely has authority to suspend refugee entry, while affirming in part preliminary injunctions requiring reception and placement services for refugees already in the US and protecting cooperative agreements with resettlement organizations; the case remains at the preliminary injunction stage.

An emergency presidential determination raised the FY2026 ceiling from 7,500 to 17,500, an increase of 10,000 for Afrikaners, citing violence incitement and disruptions to refugee processing in South Africa (published 2026-05-27).

Presidential Determination 2026-24 set the FY2027 ceiling at up to 17,500, allocated primarily to Afrikaners, with admissions still subject to Executive Order 14163's national-interest finding (published 2026-10-02).
